family.description: This family, formerly known as DUF112, is a family of bacterial and archaeal tripartite tricarboxylate transporters of the extracytoplasmic solute binding receptor-dependent transporter group of families, distinct from the ABC and TRAP-T families [[cite:PUB00106923]]. TctA is part of the tripartite TctABC system which, as characterised in S. typhimurium [[cite:PUB00106922]], is a secondary carrier that depends for activity on the extracytoplasmic tricarboxylate-binding receptor TctC as well as two integral membrane proteins, TctA and TctB. complete three-component systems are found only in bacteria. TctA is a large transmembrane protein with up to 12 predicted membrane spanning regions in bacteria and up to 11 such in archaea, with the N-terminal within the cytoplasm. TctA is thought to be a permease, and in most other bacteria functions without TctB and TctC molecules [[cite:PUB00106923]].
family.name: Tripartite tricarboxylate transporter TctA family

evidence.explanation: Original Figure4D and growth Methods distinguish the slower rise from the flat TPA/IPA curves.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: AB822591.1 tpiA CDS2015-3526 encodes E6 BAN66716.1,503aa; UniParc UPI0001DA6AF2 retains PF01970 20-441. Historical S6BBY9 is inactive/deleted as redundant. TpiA is a TctA paralog, not triosephosphate isomerase; TpiB and binding proteins are separate partners.
causal_graphs.limitations: Insertion polarity and protein abundance are unresolved. Uptake means retained radiolabel, not direct transmembrane flux. IPA/OPA/PCA uptake was not measured here. Delayed growth is not abolished growth or reduced final yield. Main text reports partial growth rescue in uninspected FigureS3; no S3 edge is added. The EME019 residual citrate signal versus near-loss in EME018 has no resolved molecular explanation.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: TctA=cg3125=NCgl2724,CAF20846 v1,510aa; UniParc UPI0000165E70 retains PF01970 20-443. Historical Q6M234 is inactive. TctB/cg3126 and TctC/cg3127 are distinct partners; CitH/cg0088 belongs to another transporter family.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole-operon rather than TctA-specific effect; strontium improvement has no resolved mechanism. Calcium-supported growth remains high. The double CitH/TctCBA mutant sometimes grows late, so no permanent universal essentiality is asserted. Neither ion stoichiometry nor direct cation-citrate cotransport was measured.

record.description: This family, formerly known as DUF112, is a family of bacterial and archaeal tripartite tricarboxylate transporters of the extracytoplasmic solute binding receptor-dependent transporter group of families, distinct from the ABC and TRAP-T families [[cite:PUB00106923]]. TctA is part of the tripartite TctABC system which, as characterised in S. typhimurium [[cite:PUB00106922]], is a secondary carrier that depends for activity on the extracytoplasmic tricarboxylate-binding receptor TctC as well as two integral membrane proteins, TctA and TctB. complete three-component systems are found only in bacteria. TctA is a large transmembrane protein with up to 12 predicted membrane spanning regions in bacteria and up to 11 such in archaea, with the N-terminal within the cytoplasm. TctA is thought to be a permease, and in most other bacteria functions without TctB and TctC molecules [[cite:PUB00106923]].

evidence.explanation: Original Figures3/4/5/7 distinguish two E6 paralogs, growth delays, tracer accumulation and joint-system conversion. Supplementary construct details remain unavailable.
Original Figures2/4 and Table3 distinguish cation-dependent operon phenotypes and a regulator-deletion transcript response; Methods and Figure2 disagree on the E. coli strain.

discussions.notes: Recover the Hosaka supplement and exact final plasmids, assess insertion polarity, and reconcile Brocker DH5alpha versus MG1655. Extend Salmonella classical transport and G109S studies, Bordetella bct systems, Pseudomonas redundancy and Gillisella tartrate contexts using exact member mapping. The2014 activated-sludge TctA_ar study inspected here is modeling rather than demonstrated citrate transport; resolve its1311bp/463aa discrepancy before sequence-level interpretation. Archived Pfam coordinates and inactive UniProt IDs are not new current profile scans. All earlier corpus follow-ups remain open.
discussions.prompt: Extend mapped TctA-family experiments while resolving constructs and transport mechanisms.
discussions.rationale: Two studies support member-specific cellular effects but do not establish isolated-domain chemistry, universal substrate specificity or ion stoichiometry.
